name: Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis Bone

criteria.description: Presence of clonal Langerhans cells with characteristic Birbeck granules on electron microscopy or CD1a/S100 positivity on immunohistochemistry
Radiographic evidence of lytic bone lesions with well-defined punched-out appearance
Localized bone pain or swelling consistent with LCH bone involvement

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathologic confirmation of Langerhans cells plus radiologic evidence of bone lesions
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires biopsy with immunohistochemical confirmation; clinical and radiologic findings support diagnosis.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Lytic bone lesions with well-demarcated borders
Clonal proliferation of Langerhans cells confirmed by CD1a and Langerin positivity

common.notes: Due to underlying lesion and inflammation

common.symptomName: Tenderness on palpation of lesion site

occasional.symptomName: Soft tissue swelling adjacent to bone lesion

rare.symptomName: Neurological deficits due to skull base involvement

rare.notes: Rare in isolated bone disease but possible in multisystem LCH

laboratory: Elevated inflammatory markers (ESR, CRP) in some cases
Normal or mildly elevated white blood cell count
imaging: X-ray showing lytic, punched-out bone lesions
CT/MRI for extent and soft tissue involvement
Bone scintigraphy may show multiple lesions
genetic: Somatic mutations in BRAF V600E in ~50% of cases
other: Histopathology showing Langerhans cells with Birbeck granules on electron microscopy
Immunohistochemistry positive for CD1a, Langerin (CD207), and S100

distinguishingFeatures: Infectious etiology with systemic signs of infection
Positive cultures or response to antibiotics
Lack of clonal Langerhans cells on biopsy
Different radiologic pattern (often mixed lytic and sclerotic)
Absence of Langerhans cells on histology
Presence of monoclonal protein in serum or urine
Plasma cells on bone marrow biopsy

references: Aricò M, et al. Langerhans cell histiocytosis in adults. Eur J Cancer. 2003.
Allen CE, et al. Langerhans-cell histiocytosis. N Engl J Med. 2018.
Badalian-Very G, et al. Recurrent BRAF mutations in Langerhans cell histiocytosis. Blood. 2010.
